selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What is the main mistake the lower self makes in this warning?
questions.answer: It acts as if life will continue for a very long time and so treats worship as something that can always be delayed.

questions.question: Which two future time periods are mentioned to show how uncertain human life is?
questions.answer: Even the next year and even the next day.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is the real reason boredom appears?
questions.answer: It comes from the illusion of endless worldly life and constant enjoyment.

questions.question: How is the daily act of worship described in terms of time?
questions.answer: It takes only a small part of the day, just one hour out of twenty-four.

questions.question: How is this act of worship described in terms of difficulty and character?
questions.answer: It is presented as beautiful, uplifting, easy, and full of mercy.

questions.question: What larger benefit is connected to spending that hour in worship?
questions.answer: It becomes a means to reach true happiness in the everlasting life.

questions.question: If a person truly understood how short life is, how would that affect his attitude toward prayer?
questions.answer: He would not resent it; instead he would feel sincere desire and joy in doing it.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about a life that passes without proper purpose?
questions.answer: It is slipping away in a wasted way.

questions.question: What contrast is being made between worldly pleasure and the hereafter?
questions.answer: Temporary enjoyment in this world is being set against lasting success in the next life.

questions.question: Who is being addressed in this warning?
questions.answer: The speaker’s own lower self.

questions.question: What question is used first to shake the lower self out of heedlessness?
questions.answer: Whether its life is everlasting.

questions.question: Why does the warning ask for proof about surviving into the future?
questions.answer: To show that the self has no certainty about how long it will live.

questions.question: What false assumption leads the self to complain?
questions.answer: It assumes it will stay in the world for a long time to enjoy itself.

questions.question: What truth about human life is presented against that assumption?
questions.answer: Human life is short and is already passing away.

questions.question: What proportion of the day is given for worship?
questions.answer: One hour from the full twenty-four hours.

questions.question: What kind of deed is that hour spent on?
questions.answer: A noble act of serving Allah that is pleasant, manageable, and compassionate in nature.

questions.question: What does this deed help a person gain?
questions.answer: Real success and happiness in eternal life.

questions.question: According to the passage, what emotional change should happen when someone understands this correctly?
questions.answer: Boredom should turn into eagerness and wholesome pleasure.

questions.question: How does the passage challenge the self’s confidence about the future?
questions.answer: It asks whether the self has any certain guarantee that it will live very long or even very soon.

questions.question: What does the self seem to want from worldly life?
questions.answer: Ongoing personal enjoyment without end.

questions.question: Why is that desire unrealistic according to the warning?
questions.answer: Because life in this world is temporary and quickly moving away.

questions.question: Why is giving one hour to worship presented as reasonable?
questions.answer: Because the cost is small while the spiritual return is immense.

questions.question: In what way is worship said to be merciful?
questions.answer: It is a compassionate means for the servant to gain lasting good, not a harsh burden.

questions.question: What shows that the warning is using cause and effect?
questions.answer: The belief in endless life causes boredom, while awareness of life’s shortness leads to motivation and joy.
